headline: The Guardian reports that women hold only a small share of new AI jobs while being more likely to work in roles that AI could disrupt.
score_reason: Matches pool score; data-backed feature, not a new event.
importance_line: It affects women in tech and customer-facing jobs, and the pay gap warning comes from advocates and a LinkedIn report rather than a long-run study.
summary: The Guardian reports, citing a LinkedIn report, that women made up about a quarter of new AI-role hires in the past year against 50% in non-AI roles, and only 13% in executive roles. Men in AI occupations earn a median of $45,000 more, partly because women are concentrated in lower-paid roles such as data annotators, and advocates warn this could widen the pay gap.
